Bitwarden CLI hit by Shai-Hulud

Target: bitwarden-cli · repo
Date: 2026-04-22 to 2026-04-23 (1 day)
Actor: TeamPCP (group)
Target Kind: application
Language: JavaScript
Cause: ci_cd_exploit
Motive: credential_theft
Transitive: true
Impact: credential_theft, self_propagation
User Impact: 0
Phase: ci_cd

Synopsis

The official Bitwarden CLI npm package (@bitwarden/cli) version 2026.4.0 was compromised during the broader Checkmarx/TeamPCP supply-chain campaign after attackers abused a GitHub Actions path in Bitwarden's CI/CD pipeline.

Story

Bitwarden CLI was hit through its npm delivery path. On April 22, 2026, version 2026.4.0 of `@bitwarden/cli` briefly carried malicious JavaScript in the package contents. The record is narrow: the CLI package on npm was affected, not Bitwarden vault data.

The payload appeared in `bw1.js` and matched the Checkmarx/TeamPCP toolchain. It used the same `audit.checkmarx.cx` telemetry endpoint, the same style of scrambled strings, and the same embedded machinery for token theft, workflow injection, and npm republishing.

The installer path mattered. The package could run through npm lifecycle behavior, scrape GitHub Actions runner memory and environment data, collect cloud and npm credentials, and use stolen publishing rights to push the campaign into more packages.

Bitwarden contained the release, revoked compromised access, and deprecated the affected npm version. The useful boundary is precise: people outside the short npm distribution window were not affected, and Bitwarden reported no evidence that end-user vault data was accessed.
